summary: Resonite is a social virtual world platform built on a live, fully reflective data model, where a wristwatch and a whole world are the same kind of object and both can be taken apart by hand while other people are standing in them. It reads more file formats than anything else in this map, covering dozens of model, image, audio, video, motion-capture, point-cloud and document types, and writes almost none of them back, so the traffic runs strongly one way; the model export wizard offers only Collada and a plain object format, the glTF transfer format it imports most cleanly is never written, and exported skinned meshes lose their bone weights and shape keys. Two things it does that almost nobody else here does deserve a standards reader's attention: every asset is named by a hash of its own bytes and fetched over an ordinary web address, which is a real shipped content-addressing system rather than an intention, and every person has a cloud inventory that follows them into any world and spawns items there. Its visual language, ProtoFlux, genuinely travels inside the exported object alongside the hierarchy, the components and the bones, which is the portable-behaviour property many standards are reaching for, but it travels only to another Resonite, because the engine, the mesh representation and the session protocol are all closed and unspecified. Four traps: the coordinate frame is left-handed with Y up, the opposite of the transfer format it reads best; the widely adopted portable avatar format VRM is explicitly unsupported on import and cannot be written at all; facial expressions use about ninety names of Resonite's own instead of either open set, while mouth shapes for speech do follow the shared fifteen-entry list; and Resonite does not run on OpenXR, the immersive session standard, targeting SteamVR and vendor runtimes instead. Content-addressed links are also unauthenticated, so holding a hash is holding the content.

coverage.note: FrooxEngine does not rasterize itself. It runs as a separate .NET process and drives a Unity renderer over inter-process communication and shared memory. The renderer is deliberately replaceable and its source is published under MIT, so a third party can in principle write a substitute renderer against the published IPC contract — but the contract only serves Resonite's own engine, it is not a general rendering standard.

coverage.note: There is no engine-level sandbox with limits. What exists is a per-world role permission system expressed as components in the world graph — Admin, Builder, Moderator, Guest, Spectator, each inheriting the one below, governing saving, spawning, transferring objects out, avatar swapping and streaming. Above that sits one coarse gate, "Unsafe Mode", which a world must opt into before experimental nodes such as writing files to disk will run, and which can be restricted by a startup-config allowlist. Below it there is nothing: no memory cap, no CPU quota, no execution timeout for guest ProtoFlux, and an impulse chain that does not yield will stall the whole engine. The documented advice for protecting content is social — do not give strangers Builder rights. Note also that Resonite's own security policy does not treat your IP address as private, because sessions are peer to peer.
